provider.notes: Registered as `elevenlabs` (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1674); live sessions build the socket client through create_stt_standard (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:420-422). The vendor has two disjoint model families: scribe_v2_realtime on a WebSocket, and scribe_v2 and scribe_v2_medical on a synchronous file endpoint. The gateway keeps one closed list of realtime ids (gateway/src/core/stt/elevenlabs/config.rs:189) and treats every other id as a file model (elevenlabs/batch.rs:63-65), which is why the provider default row is file upload. A live session that names a file model fails at setup today (config.rs:391), pinned by the test a_live_session_never_gets_the_batch_client (standard.rs:950). An empty model on a live session stays on the socket, because the configuration keeps its scribe_v2_realtime default (config.rs:331, :554-568) and the check at :391 skips an empty id; default_model records that. On the upload route an empty model resolves to scribe_v2 instead (elevenlabs/batch.rs:47), so the default depends on the route. The flat constructor ignores the configured model and always uses scribe_v2_realtime (client.rs:823-826). The spelling eleven_labs is accepted as a vendor name by the language mapper (gateway/src/core/lang/mappers/mod.rs:217) and by text-to-speech handlers (gateway/src/handlers/openai_audio.rs:1337), but not by the speech-to-text dispatcher (standard.rs:420) or the plugin registry (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1674), so it is not listed as an alias; a live session that names it does not reach this client (inferred from the dispatch arms, not run).

measurements.conditions: Pipecat constant ELEVENLABS_TTFS_P99 = 2.01 s: end of speech to final transcript for its voice-activity-segmented ElevenLabs file service, including a 200 ms detector stop delay. The Pipecat benchmark harness builds that service with scribe_v2 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pipecat-ai/stt-benchmark/main/src/stt_benchmark/services.py, reported by the real-time levers research). The constant has not changed since 2026-02-09. No median is published and the vendor publishes no latency for the file endpoint.

rates.note: Every HTTP request counts. Over the limit the vendor queues the request (about 50 ms) or answers 429 concurrent_limit_exceeded; the maximum-concurrent-requests response header carries the account's real ceiling.

context_params.note: The vendor allows 1000 entries, each under 50 characters and at most 5 words; above 100 entries every request is billed at least 20 s.

gateway_client.notes: No adapter exists. The request builder and the response parser already serve the upload route, but the driver's flush takes &mut self and runs only at disconnect, on a shared HTTP client with a 300 s timeout that is limited to HTTP/1.1 (prerecorded.rs:72, :177-185), so two uploads cannot be in flight. A live session that names a file model fails session setup with a named error (gateway/src/core/stt/elevenlabs/config.rs:391). The live request must differ from the upload route: send tag_audio_events=false (the vendor default is true and writes tokens such as (laughter) into the text; the parser removes them from the word list but not from the text, prerecorded.rs:1003-1008); send language_code when the language is known; keep timestamps_granularity=word, because per-word log-probability is the only quality signal; send at most 100 key terms and never transcript_edit. The parser hard-codes confidence 1.0 and drops language_probability and transcription_id (prerecorded.rs:1033-1048). The upload route overwrites the configured region with the driver's base URL (gateway/src/core/stt/batch.rs:776). The vendor says raw 16 kHz PCM with file_format=pcm_s16le_16 is faster than an encoded file; the builder always sends file_format=other (elevenlabs/batch.rs:488-500) and the switch waits for one live probe.

segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. The upload route's shared client allows 300 s (gateway/src/core/stt/prerecorded.rs:72); the vendor audit proposes 8 s in total and 2 s to connect, about four times the only measured P99 (2.01 s). This is an inference, not a measurement, and must be replaced once the gateway has its own numbers; how processing time grows with segment length is unknown. The container stays 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV with file_format=other until a live probe confirms the vendor's faster raw PCM option. Pre-roll, trailing silence, the 25 s maximum segment and two uploads in flight keep the defaults; the vendor's own limits (10 hours, 5 GB) never bind.

gateway_client.defect: When word timestamps are requested the vendor pairs each committed transcript with a committed_transcript_with_timestamps message and the client maps both to a turn-ending final, so one utterance probably ends the turn twice (inferred from reading, not run). The message parser does not recognise twelve of the fourteen error types the vendor documents and only logs them as unknown.
gateway_client.notes: Exercised against the vendor once: the key-gated live test elevenlabs_stt_transcribes_live drove this client through create_stt_standard with scribe_v2_realtime and got the spoken sentence back on 2026-06-04 (commit 7acd6c9, whose message records the run). That date is the last known good, not a current check. The status follows the rule the fact-check applied to the Sarvam client, which was verified by the same test file in the same commit. Since that run the WebSocket upgrade request is built by into_client_request instead of by hand, an endpoint override and a model check were added, and the shutdown signal changed (client.rs, 2026-07-12, commit 151cd1c; config.rs, up to 2026-09-25, commit 73a378a); the query parameters and the audio frame are the same (read from the diff between 7acd6c9 and the current head; messages.rs has not changed since 2026-01-18). The live test is ignored by default, is not part of CI and was not re-run, and the 2026-10-03 vendor audit made no live call, so re-run it with a working key before relying on this status. The client is also covered by unit tests of the socket URL and message parsing (gateway/src/core/stt/elevenlabs/tests.rs, run by CI) and by a mock-socket test (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:1367, not one of the test binaries CI runs). The audit found three departures from the vendor's published protocol; none is known to stop transcription: each audio chunk omits the commit and sample_rate fields that the vendor schema marks as required (messages.rs:32-39; the same omission was present in the 2026-06-04 run, which passed); the message parser recognises three of the vendor's error types (messages.rs:386) and treats the rest as unknown; and the URL builder sends no key terms, diarization, entity detection or no_verbatim. A fourth departure matters only when word timestamps are requested: the vendor then pairs every commit with a second message, committed_transcript_with_timestamps (stated in a comment in Pipecat's client, which skips the first message for that reason; read from the source file the audit fetched, not covered by the fact-check), and the gateway maps both messages to a final result that ends the turn (client.rs:488-510), so one utterance probably ends the turn twice (inferred from reading, not run). The client always asks the vendor to commit by voice-activity detection after 0.5 s of silence (config.rs:337-340; client.rs:400-431) and maps each committed transcript to a final result that also ends the turn (client.rs:488-499). It reports confidence 1.0 for a committed transcript, or a value derived from per-word log-probabilities when word timestamps were requested (client.rs:501-510). The socket accepts PCM at 8 to 48 kHz and 8 kHz mu-law. The vendor starts transcribing after the first 2 seconds of audio and closes a socket after 15 s without client messages.

gateway_client.code_ref: gateway/src/core/stt/elevenlabs/config.rs:105-113 (CommitStrategy::Manual exists; Vad is the default); gateway/src/core/stt/elevenlabs/messages.rs:32-36 (optional commit field on the audio chunk)
gateway_client.notes: Manual commit is the vendor's own default strategy: the client sends commit: true on an audio chunk and the vendor finalises the transcript, while partial transcripts keep arriving during speech. The types exist in the client, but no production code sets the manual strategy or the commit flag. The vendor commits by itself after about 36 s of accumulated audio and has a commit_throttled error type; the segmenter's 25 s maximum segment stays under that. The vendor's commit guide warns that committing manually several times in a short sequence can degrade model performance, and says that transcript processing starts after the first 2 seconds of audio; a commit at every short pause therefore needs a live test with short utterances before this transport is enabled. Use this transport when the gateway's detector should own the utterance boundary on the streaming model, so that turn timing matches segmented models.

billing.notes: Vendor price in the evidence is $0.39 per audio hour, against $0.22 for the file models. Whether a socket is billed for all streamed audio including silence is not stated outright. Two vendor sentences suggest that it is: speech-to-text is charged by the duration of the audio sent (capability page), and a keepalive has no billing impact beyond the audio already being streamed (commit guide, read in the copy of the page the audit saved). The gateway streams the whole call to this socket, silence included. gateway/src/config/pricing.rs has no elevenlabs:scribe_v2_realtime entry, so no pricing_key is set.
